accepted.s: Which case concerned mining in Odisha carried out without, or beyond, environmental clearance and directed payment of compensation equal to 100% of the value of illegally extracted minerals?
o: Noble M. Paikada v. Union of India
Common Cause v. Union of India
accepted.x: Common Cause v. Union of India (2017) concerned illegal mining in Odisha without or beyond environmental clearance. The Court directed payment of compensation equivalent to 100% of the value of the illegally extracted minerals.
accepted.tq: Match the case with its distinctive issue and monetary consequence.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Alembic Pharmaceuticals v. Rohit Prajapati:
1. It was decided in 2020.
2. The Supreme Court held that ex post facto environmental clearance was contrary to the EIA regime.
3. The 2002 Ministry of Environment and Forests circular permitting such clearance was quashed.
4. The Court necessarily directed closure of every project concerned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because compensation was imposed instead of ordering closure in every case.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong consequence in an otherwise case-specific statement set.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Noble M. Paikada v. Union of India (2024) primarily examined the validity of exemption from environmental clearance for which activity?
o: Mining in Odisha beyond the sanctioned clearance
Security projects exempted from public consultation
Extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects
accepted.x: Noble M. Paikada v. Union of India examined the 2020 exemption from environmental clearance for extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects.
accepted.tq: Use the primary-issue approach to distinguish closely related environmental cases.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court held the blanket exemption challenged in Noble M. Paikada v. Union of India to be:
o: valid only for mining in Odisha
accepted.x: The Supreme Court held the blanket exemption from environmental clearance for extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects to be arbitrary.
accepted.tq: Test the precise judicial conclusion rather than the subject matter alone.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In its May 2025 ruling in Vanashakti v. Union of India, the Supreme Court described retrospective environmental clearances as:
o: a gross illegality and an anathema to environmental law
a mandatory feature of the EIA Notification, 2006
accepted.x: The May 2025 Vanashakti ruling characterised retrospective environmental clearances as a gross illegality and an anathema to environmental law.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact judicial characterisation used in a landmark ruling.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Vanashakti litigation, consider the following statements:
1. The May 2025 ruling struck down the 2017 Notification and the 2021 Office Memorandum.
2. In November 2025, the ruling was recalled by a 2:1 majority.
3. The recall relied, among other decisions, on D. Swamy (2021) and Pahwa Plastics (2022).
4. Approximately ₹20,000 crore worth of projects was reported to be at stake.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The May 2025 ruling struck down the specified instruments, was recalled in November 2025 by a 2:1 majority, relied on the cited earlier cases, and affected projects valued at approximately ₹20,000 crore.
accepted.tq: Track multiple stages of a case without confusing the original ruling with its recall.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The final Vanashakti verdict dated 29 July 2026 was delivered by a Bench led by:
accepted.x: The final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026 was delivered by a Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant.
accepted.tq: Use the date-and-presiding-authority pair to separate successive rulings.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026?
o: It retrospectively validated all clearances obtained under the 2021 Office Memorandum.
It prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum, while earlier clearances under the 2017 Notification and 2021 Office Memorandum survived.
It made the 2017 Notification available to all fresh violators seeking regularisation.
It permanently prohibited the Centre from issuing any time-limited notification under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
accepted.x: The final verdict prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum, but earlier environmental clearances under the 2017 Notification and 2021 Office Memorandum survived. It did not open those instruments to fresh violators or permanently bar time-limited notifications under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
accepted.tq: Distinguish prospective effect, retrospective validation and future eligibility.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements concerning the legal principles stated in the final Vanashakti verdict:
1. Administrative orders cannot override the EIA Notification, 2006.
2. The Central Government may issue time-limited notifications under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
3. Ex post facto environmental clearance must satisfy Articles 14 and 21.
4. The Supreme Court retains power under Article 142.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state principles associated with the final Vanashakti verdict. Administrative orders cannot override the EIA Notification, 2006, while the stated constitutional and Article 142 principles continue to apply.
accepted.tq: Test constitutional provisions and institutional powers through a complete statement combination.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding fresh violators after the final Vanashakti verdict is NOT correct?
o: Fresh violators can automatically obtain regularisation by paying penalties under the 2021 Office Memorandum.
Fresh violators cannot seek regularisation under the 2017 Notification.
The Centre may issue time-limited notifications under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
Fresh violators cannot seek regularisation under the 2021 Standard Operating Procedure.
accepted.x: Fresh violators cannot seek regularisation under the 2017 Notification or the 2021 SOP. Automatic regularisation merely through payment of penalties under the 2021 Office Memorandum is not available to them.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that reverses the ruling’s distinction between earlier clearances and fresh violations.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which case recognised that the right to a clean environment is included within Article 21 of the Constitution?
o: Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar (1991)
Common Cause v. Union of India (2017)
Noble M. Paikada v. Union of India (2024)
accepted.x: Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar (1991) recognised that the right to a clean environment forms part of the right to life under Article 21.
accepted.tq: Link the constitutional principle with the correct case and year.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Draft EIA Notification, 2020, which combination of changes was proposed?
o: Abolition of environmental clearance and longer public consultation
Only strategic environmental assessment for all projects
Post-facto clearance and a shorter public consultation
Replacement of environmental audits by life-cycle assessments
accepted.x: The Draft EIA Notification, 2020 proposed post-facto clearance and a shorter public consultation. It was widely debated but was not finalised.
accepted.tq: Pair the proposed reform with its status and avoid treating a draft as final law.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which category of projects is exempted from public consultation under the EIA framework as determined by the Central Government?
o: Every project that has already commenced construction
All linear projects involving ordinary earth
accepted.x: Security and strategic projects may be exempted from public consultation as determined by the Central Government. The exemption is not a blanket exemption for all linear or already commenced projects.
accepted.tq: Apply the authority-and-category test to distinguish a specific executive exemption from a general one.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Environmental Impact Assessment — Combined effect of several projects in one basin
Strategic Environmental Assessment — Policies, plans and programmes upstream of projects
Life-Cycle Assessment — Compliance check of an operating unit after the fact
Environmental audit — Impacts of a product from raw material extraction to disposal
accepted.x: Strategic Environmental Assessment examines the environmental implications of policies, plans and programmes upstream of individual projects. The other descriptions refer respectively to cumulative impact assessment, environmental audit and life-cycle assessment.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure scope-pair and eliminate swapped tool definitions.
accepted.sec: EIA vs related tools - SEA, LCA, Cumulative Impact Assessment, environmental audit  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Tool)
a. Environmental Impact Assessment
b. Life-Cycle Assessment
c. Cumulative Impact Assessment
d. Environmental audit

List-II (Scope)
i. Compliance check of an operating unit after the fact
ii. A product or process across its whole life cycle
iii. A project evaluated before it starts
iv. Combined effect of several projects in one area or basin

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: EIA concerns a project before it starts; LCA covers a product or process through its life cycle; cumulative impact assessment examines combined effects; and an environmental audit checks an operating unit after the fact.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure EIA pair and complete the one-to-one matching without repeating a scope.
accepted.sec: EIA vs related tools - SEA, LCA, Cumulative Impact Assessment, environmental audit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A government is assessing the environmental implications of a new transport policy before individual road projects are selected. Which tool is most appropriate?
accepted.x: Strategic Environmental Assessment examines policies, plans and programmes upstream of individual projects. A project-level EIA is conducted for a specific project, whereas an environmental audit is generally an after-the-fact compliance check.
accepted.tq: Identify the level of decision-making before choosing between project and strategic assessment.
accepted.sec: EIA vs related tools - SEA, LCA, Cumulative Impact Assessment, environmental audit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the most appropriate tool for examining the combined environmental effects of several dams located within the same river basin?
o: Strategic Environmental Assessment of a single product
accepted.x: Cumulative Impact Assessment examines the combined effect of several projects in a defined area or basin. It is particularly suited to assessing effects that may not be apparent from separate project-level studies.
accepted.tq: Use the geographical and multi-project clues to select cumulative assessment.
accepted.sec: EIA vs related tools - SEA, LCA, Cumulative Impact Assessment, environmental audit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes EIA from LCA?
o: EIA evaluates a product from raw material to disposal, whereas LCA evaluates only a project before construction.
EIA evaluates a project before it starts, whereas LCA evaluates a product or process across its entire life cycle.
EIA is concerned with policies and programmes, whereas LCA is concerned only with public hearings.
Both EIA and LCA are compliance checks conducted only after operations begin.
accepted.x: EIA focuses on the impacts of a specific project before it starts. LCA considers the impacts of a product or process across its whole life cycle, from raw materials through disposal.
accepted.tq: Separate the object and time frame of assessment rather than treating the tools as interchangeable.
accepted.sec: EIA vs related tools - SEA, LCA, Cumulative Impact Assessment, environmental audit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The proposal for sector-wide EIAs is intended primarily to strengthen which approach?
accepted.x: Sector-wide EIAs are intended to incorporate strategic and cumulative perspectives, allowing impacts across a sector or region to be assessed rather than examining projects in isolation.
accepted.tq: Infer the broader assessment level from the phrase sector-wide.
accepted.sec: EIA vs related tools - SEA, LCA, Cumulative Impact Assessment, environmental audit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Cleaner production is best described as a strategy that:
o: Treats pollution only after it has been generated at the end of a pipe
Cuts waste and pollution at the source through process change or input substitution
Replaces environmental assessment with an operating-unit audit
Focuses exclusively on disposal of hazardous waste
accepted.x: Cleaner production is preventive: it reduces waste and pollution at source through measures such as process change and input substitution, rather than relying mainly on end-of-pipe treatment.
accepted.tq: Distinguish prevention at source from treatment after pollution is generated.
accepted.sec: Cleaner production and green chemistry - principles and link to assessment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which organisation’s mandate includes encouraging cleaner production technologies?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board’s mandate includes encouraging cleaner production technologies.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional mandate with the correct environmental body.
accepted.sec: Cleaner production and green chemistry - principles and link to assessment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Green chemistry primarily involves designing products and processes that:
o: Reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances
Increase the use of hazardous substances for higher efficiency
Transfer all pollution from production to disposal
Avoid consideration of raw materials and solvents
accepted.x: Green chemistry seeks to design products and processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances. It addresses environmental impacts at the design stage rather than merely treating pollution later.
accepted.tq: Choose the preventive design objective instead of an end-of-pipe measure.
accepted.sec: Cleaner production and green chemistry - principles and link to assessment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The twelve principles of green chemistry were formulated by:
o: The Supreme Court in Subhash Kumar (1991)
The Central Government under the EIA Notification, 2006
accepted.x: The twelve principles of green chemistry are associated with Paul Anastas and John Warner and were formulated in 1998.
accepted.tq: Use the author-year association to avoid confusing principles with legal notifications or judgments.
accepted.sec: Cleaner production and green chemistry - principles and link to assessment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a principle or example associated with green chemistry?
accepted.x: Green chemistry promotes prevention of waste, atom economy and safer solvents. Maximising hazardous by-products is contrary to its objective.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the preventive and hazard-reduction objective.
accepted.sec: Cleaner production and green chemistry - principles and link to assessment  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Renewable feedstocks are associated with green chemistry.
2. Designing products for degradation is an example of a green chemistry principle.
3. Cleaner production relies exclusively on end-of-pipe treatment.
4. Both cleaner production and green chemistry seek to reduce impacts at the design stage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because cleaner production is preventive and seeks process or input changes at the source rather than relying exclusively on end-of-pipe treatment.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme word exclusively and combine the related design-stage principles.
accepted.sec: Cleaner production and green chemistry - principles and link to assessment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How do cleaner production and green chemistry relate to EIA and LCA?
o: They increase residual impacts so that EIA and LCA can identify more mitigation measures.
They eliminate the need to assess alternatives in location and process technology.
They make EIA applicable only after a project has started.
They shrink impacts at the design stage, enabling EIA and LCA to find fewer residual impacts requiring mitigation.
accepted.x: Cleaner production and green chemistry reduce impacts during design, so EIA and LCA identify fewer residual impacts that require mitigation. EIA nevertheless continues to require assessment of alternatives in location and process technology.
accepted.tq: Test the causal link between preventive design and the residual-impact stage of assessment.
accepted.sec: Cleaner production and green chemistry - principles and link to assessment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the context of environmental clearance, which of the following is the correct general rule?
o: Prior clearance is required only for products assessed through LCA.
Environmental clearance is needed only after an environmental audit identifies non-compliance.
Prior environmental clearance is mandatory under the EIA framework, while post-facto approval is only a narrow exception.
Post-facto approval is the normal rule and prior clearance is optional.
accepted.x: The general rule under the EIA framework is that prior environmental clearance is mandatory. Post-facto approval, where recognised at all, is treated only as a narrow exception.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the governing rule from exceptional regularisation mechanisms.
accepted.sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]
